title: Warning Out in New England, 1656-1817
author: Josiah Henry Benton
source_url: https://archive.org/details/warningoutinnewe00bent (OCR text: https://archive.org/download/warningoutinnewe00bent/warningoutinnewe00bent_djvu.txt; Boston: W. B. Clarke Company, 1911)
notes: Complete text, chapters I-VII and the Chronology (title pages, contents and index omitted). Chapters: I introduction and examples of warning out, inhabitancy, land titles; II admission of inhabitants and town grants; III Massachusetts colony and state laws; IV Connecticut; V New Hampshire colony and state laws; VI Rhode Island; VII how long warning out was practised (incl. Vermont, and the settlement acts that ended it). Cleaned from the archive.org OCR: running heads removed, page numbers kept as [p. N], hyphenation joined; footnotes collected at the end of each chapter under **Notes** as '(p. N) marker text' (OCR renders the dagger/double-dagger markers as t/f/X). Benton quotes many town records and statutes in their original spelling; residual OCR misreadings are occasional.

title: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Parents, and the Duty of Parents towards their Children (An Exposition of the Fifth Commandement)
author: Thomas Cobbet (Cobbett), minister of Lynn, Massachusetts
source_url: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/textcreationpartnership/A33522/master/A33522.xml (EEBO-TCP A33522; London: printed by S.G. for John Rothwell, 1656)
license: CC0 1.0 (EEBO-TCP Phase II keyed text); underlying work public domain
notes: Complete body of the treatise, chapters I-VII (honour in general; respect and love; reverence; obedience; recompence/thankfulness incl. children's maintenance and service of needy parents, 'as with us generally in New England'; honour in a reflect way). Front matter (title page, epistles) omitted. [p. N] = page of the 1656 print; [margin: ...] = marginal notes; 〈…〉 = illegible or Greek/Hebrew not keyed by TCP. Long s converted to s.

title: Whereas the Lawes published by the Honoured General Court ... do require all Townes from time to time to dispose of Single Persons and inmates within their Towns to Service (order to constables on family government)
author: Massachusetts Bay General Court
license: CC0 1.0 (Evans-TCP keyed text); underlying work public domain
notes: Complete broadside as transcribed by TCP (text ends at 'Returne to the next Court' in the TCP transcription). Orders constables to list young persons living 'from under family Government' and requires selectmen to enforce the laws placing single persons in families (Lib. 1 p. 76 sect. 3; Children and Youth p. 16).

title: The Massachusetts Body of Liberties (The Liberties of the Massachusets Collonie in New England)
author: General Court of Massachusetts Bay (drafted by Nathaniel Ward)
source_url: https://history.hanover.edu/texts/masslib.html (Hanover Historical Texts Project transcription of Old South Leaflets, vol. 7, pp. 261-280, c. 1900, which follows the manuscript printed by W. H. Whitmore, Colonial Laws of Massachusetts, 1889)
notes: Complete text, 98 numbered liberties. # = the code's own group headings (Liberties of Women 79-80; of Children 81-84 incl. 81 the eldest son's double portion on intestacy and 83 redress against parents who deny timely marriage; of Servants 85-88; of Foreigners and Strangers 89-91). Capital laws numbered 94.1-94.12 and church liberties 95.1-95.11 as in the source. Leaflet page numbers and the leaflet's editorial notes omitted. Wording spot-checked against Whitmore 1889 (archive.org coloniallawsofma00mass).

title: The General Laws and Liberties of the Massachusets Colony, revised and re-printed 1672: selected titles on family, household government, marriage, servants, the poor, strangers, dower and inheritance
author: Massachusetts Bay General Court (ed. Edward Rawson, secretary)
date_of_work: 1672 (laws enacted 1641-1672; revision of the 1648 Book of the General Lawes and Libertyes and 1660 edition)
source_url: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/textcreationpartnership/N00114/master/N00114.xml (Evans-TCP N00114; Evans 168; Wing M1003; Cambridge: Samuel Green, 1672)
license: CC0 1.0 (Evans-TCP keyed text); underlying work public domain
notes: Titles included: Ability/Age; Age for plaintiffs; Capital Laws (incl. cursing/smiting parents, stubborn and rebellious son); Children and Youth (education, catechising, calling, placing out of neglected children, parental denial of marriage, orphans); Dowries (widow's thirds); Escheats; Fornication (incl. bastardy orders); Idle Persons; Lands free Lands; Liberties Common; Marriages and Married Persons; Masters, Servants, Labourers; Poor; Records (births, marriages, deaths); Schools; Strangers (entertaining strangers, settlement); Town-ship; Vagabonds; Wills (incl. Sect. 3: widow's part and eldest son's double portion on intestacy). # = the code's own titles; ## Sect. N = its numbered sections (first section of each title is unnumbered in the print). Bracketed years [1641] etc. are the enactment dates printed in the code. [p. N] = page of the 1672 edition. [margin: ...] = printed marginal notes. A clean public-domain text of the 1648 edition itself was not available; the 1672 revision carries the same titles forward.

title: The Book of the General Laws of the Inhabitants of the Jurisdiction of New-Plimouth (1672): chapters I, II, VIII, IX, X (Fundamentals; Capital Laws; Ministers' Maintenance with Education of Children, Mispending of Time, Marriages; Town Affairs incl. the poor and inhabitants; Lands, Inheritances and Wills)
author: New Plymouth Colony General Court
source_url: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/textcreationpartnership/N00116/master/N00116.xml (Evans-TCP N00116; Evans 171; Wing N711; Cambridge: Samuel Green, 1672)
license: CC0 1.0 (Evans-TCP keyed text); underlying work public domain
notes: # = chapter, ## = the printed sub-titles within chapters; numbered paragraphs keep the code's own numbers. [p. N] = page of the 1672 print; [margin: ...] = marginal notes; 〈…〉 = illegible in the scan. Includes the order that selectmen list 'single persons that live from under Family Government' (ch. title: Provincial poor-law extracts: Massachusetts Bay 1692-3 ch. 28 ss. 8-10 and New Hampshire 1719 ch. 12 (inhabitancy by three months' residence unless warned out; relations in the line of father, grandfather, mother, grandmother, children and grandchildren to relieve the impotent poor; removal of persons warned out)
author: General Court of the Province of the Massachusetts Bay; General Assembly of the Province of New Hampshire
source_url: https://archive.org/details/actsresolvespubl_d01mass (Acts and Resolves, Public and Private, of the Province of the Massachusetts Bay, vol. 1, Boston 1869, pp. 67-68) ; https://archive.org/details/lawsofnewhampshi02newh (Laws of New Hampshire, vol. 2, Province Period 1702-1745, ed. A. S. Batchellor, Concord 1913, pp. 343-344)
license: Public domain (colonial statutes; 1869 and 1913 state publications)
notes: Extracts only: the sections of each act dealing with inhabitancy, warning out, removal and the relatives' duty of support. Hand-corrected from the archive.org OCR (marginal notes and case citations of the 1869 edition omitted; editorial brackets of the editions kept, e.g. [or] [and], precinct[s]). Superscript abbreviations of the NH manuscript text rendered with ^ (afors^d = aforesaid). The Massachusetts act sets the penalty at 20s a month and adds grandchildren to the English list of 43 Eliz. c. 2; New Hampshire copies it with a 30s penalty. Later state statutes (Massachusetts 1793-4, New Hampshire 1791/1796, Vermont 1797/1817) were not extracted: no clean public-domain text was obtained in the time available.

notes: Only the fifth-commandment lectures on family and age relations; the lectures on civil rulers, ministers and other political orders (Sermons CLXXXI-CLXXXVII) are omitted. # = sermon. [p. title: Laws of Vermont, February 1779 (first code): acts on marriage, the poor and relatives' support, warning out, guardianship, and the distribution of estates
author: Vermont. General Assembly
notes: Twelve acts of the February 1779 session, from Slade's Vermont State Papers (1823), pp. ~288-380. Text built from four independent archive.org OCRs of the 1823 book (vermontstatepape00verm as base; vermontstatepape1779verm, vermontstatepap01statgoog, vermontstatepap00statgoog) by word-level majority vote, then hand-corrected for remaining OCR errors; running heads and page numbers removed, line-end hyphens rejoined. Spelling as printed (impowered, goal, cloaths, select-men). Not yet compared word-for-word with page images. The 1797 and 1808 compilations were not used: the only archive.org copy of the 1797 revision (ECCO scan, 1798) has unusable long-s OCR.
